description: Rework the dashboard into an attention-first production overview: needs-attention model absorbs runner state, active production becomes issue-led with stage + owner-action cue, and the page becomes a priority stack with a capacity level, collapsing empty zones and a concise ready state. Web-only, no backend change.

tasks.title: Evolve needs-attention model to absorb runner state and render uniformly in the hero
tasks.description: Evolve AttentionItem from a flat interface into a discriminated union of issue kinds (approval-needed/integration-failed/interrupted/blocked, carrying issueNumber+issueId) and runner kinds (runner-unavailable/runner-capacity-limited, no issue reference). Make deriveAttentionItems consume its agentStatus argument (currently ignored) and emit runner-unavailable when runnerAvailable === false and runner-capacity-limited when runnerAvailable !== false && max > 0 && active >= max, with runner-unavailable suppressing capacity-limited and runner items sorting after issue items. Update attention-treatment.ts to route the two runner kinds through statusTreatment (unavailable -> danger/solid glyph matching today's RunnerDownEntry, capacity-limited -> warning). Delete AttentionHero's special-cased RunnerDownEntry and render runner items uniformly from the model, preserving the runner-down-entry/-message/-link test-ids for the unavailable kind.
acceptanceCriteria: deriveAttentionItems(issues, agentStatus) emits runner-unavailable when runnerAvailable === false, even when the issue array is empty
deriveAttentionItems emits runner-capacity-limited iff runnerAvailable !== false && max > 0 && active >= max; it does not fire when active < max or when max === 0
runner-unavailable suppresses runner-capacity-limited (the two are never emitted together)
Runner items are emitted after issue items; the issue classification order (approval -> integration-failed -> interrupted -> blocked, first-match-wins, dedup by id) is unchanged
AttentionItem is a discriminated union: issue items carry issueNumber/issueId, runner items do not, and the kind set is exhaustive
AttentionHero renders runner items from the model; the RunnerDownEntry special-case is removed; runner-down-entry/-message/-link test-ids are preserved for the unavailable kind
attention.test.ts (unit) covers all runner-item scenarios above and inverts the existing 'agentStatus is ignored' assertion (agentStatus is now consumed)
AttentionHero.test.tsx (spec) asserts runner-capacity-limited surfaces as an attention item under saturation and runner-unavailable still surfaces
tasks.output: Updated entities/issue/model/attention.ts, entities/issue/lib/attention-treatment.ts, widgets/attention-hero/ui/AttentionHero.tsx; updated attention.test.ts and AttentionHero.test.tsx
tasks.notes: Implements design D1/D2. Single source of every needs-attention state; removes the model-vs-hero two-path split. Default/fallback agentStatus (no runnerAvailable) is treated as runner-up and fires neither runner item, preserving the loading-path behavior. Verify with: npm run typecheck -w packages/web && npm run test:run -w packages/web.

tasks.title: Rework active-production zone to be issue-led with workflow stage and owner-action cue
tasks.description: Rework PulseZone to enumerate running issues (status === IssueStatus.InProgress && health !== 'done' && health !== 'cancelled', sourced from useIssues — the same in-flight predicate factory-status uses) instead of active agent sessions. Each row shows the issue title with a link to /issues/{number}, its current workflowStage rendered with the categorical stage-identity palette already in CompactSessionCard, and an owner-action-needed cue when the issue also produces an attention item. Factor issueNeedsOwnerAction(issue) as a shared predicate used by both the cue and deriveAttentionItems so they can never disagree. Join optional session telemetry (tokens, task progress, context health) from useActivityCards by issue number when an active session exists; rows without a session render with stage + cue only so paused work stays visible. Remove the capacity header (pulse-slots / pulse-capacity-header) from PulseZone since capacity relocates to its own dashboard level in T-003.
acceptanceCriteria: An in-progress issue with no active agent session stays visible in PulseZone with its current workflow stage
Each running-issue row displays its current workflowStage using the categorical stage-identity palette
A running issue that needs owner action (awaiting approval / blocked / interrupted / integration-failed) shows a cue distinguishing it from an issue running normally
issueNeedsOwnerAction(issue) is a single shared predicate used by both the inline cue and deriveAttentionItems, so the cue and the attention entry never disagree
Active session telemetry enriches the matching running-issue row by issue number when a session exists; a missing session does not hide the issue
pulse-compact-* test-ids are preserved
PulseZone no longer renders pulse-slots / pulse-capacity-header

PulseZone.test.tsx is rewritten for the issue-led model: paused issue visible with stage, owner-action cue distinguishes action-needed from normally-running, active sessions enrich matching issues, capacity header is absent
tasks.output: Updated widgets/dashboard-pulse/ui/PulseZone.tsx, widgets/dashboard-pulse/ui/CompactSessionCard.tsx, widgets/coder-session/model/activity-cards.ts; new shared issueNeedsOwnerAction predicate; rewritten PulseZone.test.tsx
tasks.notes: Implements design D4. Depends on T-001 for the shared issueNeedsOwnerAction predicate (co-located with the attention model). Capacity usage display relocates to the capacity level built in T-003; until then the capacity-limited attention item from T-001 still surfaces runner saturation. Verify with: npm run typecheck -w packages/web && npm run test:run -w packages/web.

tasks.title: Establish attention-first zone hierarchy with capacity level, collapse, and ready state
tasks.description: Rewrite DashboardPage into an explicit priority stack: headline (always, compact strip) -> attention (render iff hasAttention) -> active-production (render iff hasActiveWork: running issues or active sessions) -> capacity (render iff max > 0) -> recent-history (render iff digest has items). Create the capacity level (dashboard-zone-capacity) as a compact usage strip sourced from agentStatus.capacity, which collapses (renders nothing) when max === 0 or capacity data is absent. Remove DashboardZone's fixed min-h-[160px] so zones size to content and return null when empty (structural collapse). Compute hasAttention and hasActiveWork once in DashboardPage from the shared hooks (useIssues, useAgentStatus) and the same predicates used by the hero and pulse so the page cannot disagree with its children. Render a concise ready state when !hasAttention && !hasActiveWork instead of the hero-plus-empty-boxes layout, keeping the headline as the compact strip above it and allowing the digest to appear as a small subordinate strip when it has items. Assert the factory-status headline stays subordinate to the attention zone.
acceptanceCriteria: The four levels render in priority order (attention before active-production before capacity before recent-history), verifiable via compareDocumentPosition in DashboardPage.test.tsx
Runner capacity usage appears as its own dashboard-zone-capacity level, separate from active-production and recent-history, sourced from agentStatus.capacity
The capacity level collapses (is not rendered) when max === 0 or capacity data is absent
An empty lower-priority zone is absent from the DOM when higher-priority content exists (no reserved fixed-height box)
DashboardZone no longer forces min-h-[160px]; zones size to content
When there are no needs-attention states and no running/active issues, a concise ready state renders instead of empty fixed-height zones
hasAttention and hasActiveWork are computed once in DashboardPage from the same predicates/hooks used by the hero and pulse
The factory-status headline precedes the attention zone and is not more visually prominent than it (subordinate compact strip)
Stable test-ids are preserved (dashboard-zone-attention/-pulse/-digest, dashboard-zone-capacity, factory-status-headline)

DashboardPage.test.tsx (spec) covers: zone priority order via compareDocumentPosition, empty-zone collapse when higher-priority content exists, concise ready state when idle, capacity level rendering and collapse, and headline subordination
tasks.output: Rewritten pages/dashboard/ui/DashboardPage.tsx; updated pages/dashboard/ui/DashboardZone.tsx; new capacity-level surface (dashboard-zone-capacity); rewritten DashboardPage.test.tsx
tasks.notes: Implements design D3/D5/D6. Completes capacity-feed unification (last consumer of AgentActivity.summary.slots for capacity is removed). After completion, manually sweep the four dashboard states (has-attention, active-only, idle/ready, capacity-limited) in light and dark theme. Verify with: npm run typecheck -w packages/web && npm run test:run -w packages/web.
